jobs.description:
**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic.

The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research. We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch.

You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next.

We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships. We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way.

The shape of the role is flexible. You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly. Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both. Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time.

What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on.

This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding. If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you.

**Key responsibilities**
------------------------

* Design, build, and maintain biology software in genomics and structural biology (libraries, command-line tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks) for use by researchers and AI agents, inside Anthropic and externally
* Own the path from research code to public release, including testing, validation against reference data and established tools, benchmarking, documentation, and packaging, and make the call on when something is ready to ship
* Maintain what we release: triage issues, review outside contributions, and manage breaking changes
* Represent the team in the biology community through conferences, workshops, tutorials, and direct work with researchers and maintainers, and turn what you learn about their needs into priorities for the team
* Partner with the team's computational and experimental scientists to turn research code into well-tested, reusable software
* Lead the technical direction of the projects you own through design review, code review, and mentoring, and, depending on your interests and the team's needs, lead a small team
* Build with Claude and AI coding agents as your default way of working, hold agent-written code to the same standard as your own, and set the team's practices for reviewing and validating it

**Minimum qualifications**
--------------------------

* Have built, released, and maintained biology software that researchers outside your own group use, with evidence of adoption you can point to (for example public repositories, package downloads, citations, or use in other groups' pipelines)
* Have deep working expertise in genomics or structural biology, including the data types, file formats, standard tools, and common failure modes of at least one of these fields
* Are proficient in Python and comfortable working with large datasets in Linux and cloud or cluster computing environments
* Practice rigorous testing and release engineering: unit and integration tests, continuous integration, validation against reference data, packaging, and versioning
* Use AI coding tools as a central part of how you build software, and can show how you verify the correctness and performance of code you did not write by hand
* Have led a technical project with multiple contributors, setting direction and reviewing others' work while continuing to write code yourself
* Can explain technical work clearly to both biologists and engineers, in writing (documentation, tutorials) and in person (talks, workshops)

**Preferred qualifications**
----------------------------

* Depth in both genomics and structural biology
* A record as the creator or a core maintainer of a widely used open-source tool in computational biology
* Experience managing or formally leading a team of engineers or scientists
* A graduate degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent experience
* Proficiency in a systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and experience with performance work on large biological datasets
* Experience building software in other areas of computational biology, such as phylogen

**Cal Poly Pomona Enterprises Employment Services**

  

**ANNOUNCEMENT OF POSITION VACANCY**

  

**SUMMARY**: Graduate Research Assistant - Food Bioprocessing and Smart Manufacturing The Department of Nutrition and Food Science is seeking two motivated graduate students to join a collaborative research program led by Dr. Mohammad Zarei. The positions are supported through the NSF Center for Research Advancement in Smart Manufacturing (CREST-RASM) and connect hands-on food-science experimentation with process monitoring, data analysis, modeling, and digital-twin validation. Students will work with food science and engineering collaborators and contribute to publishable research in sustainable food manufacturing. Current projects include the valorization of tomato seed meal, sorghum distillers dried grains with solubles (DDGS), and California alfalfa through enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation. These are representative projects rather than the limits of the appointment. Depending on project needs and student interests, assignments may also involve alternative and plant proteins, agricultural and food by-product biorefineries, extrusion processing, bioactive peptides, sustainable packaging and bioplastics, functional foods, downstream processing, cultivated-food applications, and AI-assisted process optimization

  

**RESEARCH AREAS AND POTENTIAL ASSIGNMENTS**

* Food bioprocessing and biorefinery systems: protein extraction, concentration, enzymatic hydrolysis, fermentation, separation, and recovery.

* Alternative proteins and value-added ingredients: plant proteins, protein hydrolysates, bioactive peptides, functional ingredients, and applications in food or feed.

* Smart food manufacturing: real-time monitoring, sensor data, experimental design, process optimization, and validation of data-driven or digital-twin models.

* Food process engineering and sustainable materials: extrusion, ingredient functionality, texture and rheology, bioplastics, and sustainable packaging when relevant to active projects.

  

**SOME OF THE THINGS THAT YOU WILL GET TO DO (this is just a small sampling of work variety):**

* Plan and conduct laboratory experiments under approved protocols, including preparation of raw materials, reagents, enzymes, cultures, and samples.

* Assist with protein extraction, hydrolysis, fermentation, extrusion, fractionation, purification, and functional or bioactivity testing, depending on project assignment.

* Operate and help maintain research equipment such as stirred-tank bioreactors, the Labfors 5 and Eppendorf SciVario Twin platforms, twin-screw extrusion systems, texture and viscosity instruments, and other analytical tools after training.

**Position Summary**

We are seeking a detail-oriented Chemical Laboratory Technician to support and maintain chemical process controls for aerospace surface treatment operations.

The Chemical Lab Technician will be responsible for sampling, testing, analyzing, documenting, and monitoring chemical solutions used in processes such as anodizing, passivation, cleaning, etching, conversion coating, and other chemical finishing operations.

The technician will perform routine laboratory analysis of process tanks, verify that chemical concentrations and operating parameters remain within established specifications, identify out-of-control conditions, and work closely with Engineering, Quality, and Production to maintain stable and compliant chemical processes.

This position requires strong attention to detail, disciplined laboratory practices, accurate documentation, and strict adherence to chemical safety requirements.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Collect representative samples from chemical processing tanks according to established sampling frequencies and procedures.
* Perform routine chemical analysis of production solutions used for:
  + Anodizing
  + Passivation
  + Cleaning and degreasing
  + Acid etching
  + Deoxidizing/desmutting
  + Conversion coating and other chemical finishing processes
* Test and monitor solutions that may contain or involve acids such as hydrofluoric acid, nitric acid, and mixed acid solutions, as applicable to approved company processes.
* Perform chemical concentration testing using laboratory techniques such as titration, pH measurement, conductivity measurement, specific gravity/density testing, and other analytical methods required by applicable process specifications.
* Monitor chemical bath parameters including concentration, contamination levels, pH, temperature, conductivity, and other specified characteristics.
* Compare analytical results against established process specifications, control limits, and operating ranges.
* Immediately identify and communicate out-of-specification or abnormal chemical conditions to Engineering, Quality, and Production.
* Calculate required chemical additions or adjustments according to approved procedures and established process controls.

### **Company Description**

**Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!**

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

### **Job Description**

The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security.

We have openings in Summer 2027 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security.

*This position offers a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. You will have the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week.*

CGSR’s objectives are as follows:

* To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts.
* To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term.
* To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security.
* To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment.
* To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment.

More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/.

This job will be closed to applicants on February 1, 2027.

**You will**

* Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff.
* Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports.

**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic.

The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research. We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community. Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well. Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch.

You'll own that standard. You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it. You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next.

We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships.
